newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds Metals says may not meet asset sale goal.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds Metals says may not meet asset sale goal.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co CEO Jeremiah Sheehan said on Wednesday that the company was not likely to meet a self-imposed end-of-June deadline for completing asset sales as part of a major restructuring program.

"My goal is to get them all signed, not necessarily closed, by the end of June. I'm not sure we'll accomplish that," Sheehan told reporters after speaking at the Aluminum Association's Alumitech 1997 forum here.
"I think I can say for sure we'll get them all done this year."
Sheehan said asset sales had been slowed by the unexpected length of discussions involving some properties which have drawn interest from as many as five prospective buyers.
"Some of them take a little longer than others in terms of discussing with people, especially if you have four or five different people interested," he said.
He did not say what asset sales were taking longest to negotiate, nor did he say which assets had drawn the most interest.

Sheehan said Reynolds Metals' top priority is to get managers focused on key business areas, namely base materials, construction, transportation, cans, flexible packaging, distribution and emerging markets.

He said company executives had made no decision on whether to spin off Reynolds' packaging operation. He said that although such a step would be welcomed by Wall Street, the company had "tax situations" to consider.
"But also we want to make sure the company that's left can get through the down cycle years," Sheehan said.
He said it would be the end of the year before Reynolds Metals was in a position to concentrate solely on its future business plan without also being distracted by the ongoing restructuring.

"The top priority is to get our new organization set and what we're trying to do is get the managers of these business units focused on going forward and keep a separate management team working on the restructuring," Sheehan explained.

He said Reynolds Metals' long-term objective was to concentrate on emerging markets including China, Russia and India. But he emphasized that the company was pursuing a cautious strategy, saying Reynolds did not want to "rush in with big investments."
He added that the company was "not anxious to put a lot of cash into Russia."
"The world is outside of North America and Europe, and that's where we have to concentrate in the future," he said.
